"In this particular instance, rape is not necessary to Sansa’s character development,"

I have to ask this because I've only read the books. Does Sansa actually have character development in the show? That seems like a bigger break from the books than a rape scene.

In the show she's consistently been protected and used as a pawn by various other characters, with no real interesting actions of her own. I think the development they're hinting at is that they may actually turn her into a more proactive character. Guess we'll see, she's been pretty useless so far.

In the show she's consistently been protected and used as a pawn by various other characters, with no real interesting actions of her own.

That is the development. She started out the series as a young, naive girl living as a noble in a sheltered outlying castle. The entire series has been her losing everything, being broken down, tossed around, and yes: used. At every point... when she lost her home, father, mother, siblings, even being sidelined from marriage by Joffrey... every single time she lost something, there was a moment of resolve, where she found some emotion or some new line of thinking that has made her stronger and stronger. Do you think that if the events of the Eyrie had happened in Season 1 that she would have had the forethought or guile to stand up for herself to play along with Littlefinger's games? Do you think if the rape had happened in Season 1 that she would have laid there silently gritting her teeth?

Every single thing that has happened to her, every loss she has had, has been about breaking down her naivety and building her into a competitor... someone who can play politics with the rest of the series heavy hitters. Her "virtue" was the last thing she had tying her to childhood and innocence. And now she is going to be the Lady of Winterfell with the might of House Bolton behind her. I foresee her pulling off some sort of badassery coming up.

Do you think that if the events of the Eyrie had happened in Season 1 that she would have had the forethought or guile to stand up for herself to play along with Littlefinger's games? Do you think if the rape had happened in Season 1 that she would have laid there silently gritting her teeth?

Perhaps it's portrayed differently in the books, but in the show her attitude toward Littlefinger seems no different than the deference that she grudgingly showed to Joffrey. I guess you're proposing that laying there silently while being raped is a courageous tactic, but finding a way to avoid being raped would have been the route favored by anyone with a backbone.

The one thing I will give her credit for is being sassy to the Bolton's at dinner and such - calling it her home, etc. - unfortunately her actions aren't matching up to her mouth yet. Like you though, I would expect that will change eventually - I just hope it's sooner rather than later, because she's been utterly boring so far.
